clue.text: (& 23dn./26ac.) Orgasm complete, rotate and go back to the start

blocks.note: slang verb for reaching orgasm
complete or entire
to circle is to go round

explanation.surface: A smutty Private Eye picture of a sexual climax followed by rolling over and starting all over again.
explanation.walkthrough: The rude opening reads as a story, but each word is a plain synonym laid end to end; 'go back to the start' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes returning, after a series of developments, to the original position or situation.

clue.text: A natural for PM role? 'Boris is out' (Guardian's last editorial)

indicators.note: something out is no longer present, so the named letters are removed
the last of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the name as written, before trimming
the two letters taken away from the name
final letter of the newspaper's name
a newspaper's leader is its editorial column

explanation.surface: A newspaper editorial cheering that Boris Johnson is gone, wondering who might be a natural to take over as Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boris is out' means BORIS with IS removed, giving BOR. In British papers a leader is the editorial opinion piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with innate gifts for command would be an obvious, instinctive choice to head a government.

clue.text: (& 4/25dn.) Tory ex-cabinet minister failing, as feared – as will pleas to politicians to sort Brexit?

definitions.text: as will pleas to politicians to sort Brexit
definitions.note: the definition is a sentence frame: pleas will FALL ON DEAF EARS

indicators.note: a failing thing is breaking down, so its letters fall into disorder

blocks.note: Michael Fallon, former Conservative Defence Secretary
the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A disgraced Tory minister fails as everyone feared, much like public pleading for Westminster to fix Brexit.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Fallon resigned as Defence Secretary in 2017; Tory means Conservative. The definition reads as a sentence completion: pleas will fall on deaf ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Requests that fall on deaf ears are ignored, which is the cynical expectation for appeals to politicians over Brexit.

clue.text: see 3dn.
John had to sign it after Armagnac drunk, thanks

indicators.note: a drunk is unsteady and muddled, so the letters stagger into a new order

blocks.note: the brandy's name, to be rearranged
ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: Someone called John signs a document only after a glass of brandy, then says thank you.
explanation.walkthrough: John is King John, forced by his barons to seal the charter at Runnymede in 1215.
explanation.definitionFit: King John was compelled by rebel barons to agree the 1215 charter limiting royal power.

clue.text: Support like this overturned failed presidential candidate's motion

indicators.note: something overturned is flipped end over end, so its letters run backwards

blocks.note: a prop holds something up
so means in this way
Al Gore, who lost the 2000 US election

explanation.surface: Backing for a motion put forward by a defeated presidential hopeful, which then gets overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overturned' looks like it acts on the candidate's motion, but it only flips the short word before it. Al Gore is the standard failed candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: In a meeting or debate, a motion is a formal suggestion put forward for a vote.

clue.text: Scoffs: "politician lacks alternative – dump!"

indicators.note: to lack something is to be without it, so those letters go missing

blocks.note: to pig is to eat greedily
a Conservative politician
the word offering an alternative

explanation.surface: Someone sneers that a politician has no other option but to be thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffs' reads as mocks, but here it means eats greedily. TORY without OR leaves TY.
explanation.definitionFit: A filthy, squalid place is informally called a dump, just like an animal pen for swine.

clue.text: Announcer heard waffling about "lousy start"

indicators.note: waffling speech rambles without order, so the letters are jumbled
about means around, so one piece goes round another
the start of a word is its opening letter alone

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged
opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A broadcaster is overheard rambling on about a poor beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heard' looks like the past tense of hear in the surface, but it supplies the letters; the rearranged HERAD wraps the L.
explanation.definitionFit: A herald was an official messenger who proclaimed news, so the word names someone making announcements.

clue.text: For use of hospital patients not in the dark?

definitions.text: For use of hospital patients not in the dark?

blocks.clueFragment: For use of hospital patients not in the dark?
blocks.note: surface reading: something for patients who are kept informed

blocks.clueFragment: hospital patients not in the dark
blocks.note: setter's reading: day patients, who are not kept overnight, need a couch for daytime rest

explanation.walkthrough: 'Not in the dark' suggests patients told about their condition; it really means patients there in daylight only, not overnight.

clue.text: 'Pet' Nigel, recklessly blowing top, holds back Britain

indicators.note: losing the top means the head is removed, so the opening letter goes
acting recklessly means without care or order, so letters scatter
going back means running the other way, so letters are read in reverse
to hold is to grip inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: the name, which loses its first letter before being mixed
BR is the abbreviation for Britain

explanation.surface: Nigel Farage, called someone's pet, loses his temper wildly while trying to hold Britain back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' in quotes looks like a nickname for Nigel, but it is the definition. Blowing his top sounds like losing his temper; here it beheads the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A gerbil is a small desert rodent commonly kept as a household animal companion.

clue.text: Maybe Philip gets depressed in shade

blocks.note: Sir Philip Green, the retail tycoon behind BHS and Topshop, is one example of a Green
feeling blue is feeling low

explanation.surface: Philip, perhaps a fallen businessman, becomes downcast and retreats into the shadows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' signals an example: Philip is one person surnamed Green, the British retailer whose BHS chain collapsed in 2016.
explanation.definitionFit: A colour midway between two primary hues is a particular tint or shade of colour.

clue.text: Fashionable sport, knocking the stuffing out of Kerry

indicators.note: removing the stuffing empties the middle, so only the outside letters stay

blocks.note: sport in the sense of amusement or play
first and last letters of the name

explanation.surface: A trendy game sees someone beat Kerry soundly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' looks like a game to be played, but it means fun, as in 'it was great sport'.
explanation.definitionFit: Funky is informal slang for stylish, modern and cool, much like trendy or hip.

clue.text: Being pissed, I daren't do a commercial deal

indicators.note: a drunken person is all over the place, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: the seven letters to be rearranged, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A drunk businessman refuses to sign any deal while under the influence.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'pissed' means drunk, not angry, which is why it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To trade in is to hand over goods as part payment, so it is a kind of business transaction.

clue.text: Frank's too grand for meal provision

blocks.note: if you are too grand for something you are above it
board is food supplied, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A snobbish man called Frank is too posh for the food on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name, but it is an adjective meaning open and honest, and the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dealings that are open, honest and without concealment are described with this idiom.

clue.text: F-off, tucking into cheese roll

indicators.note: tucking into something puts you inside it, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: och is a Scottish exclamation of irritation or dismissal
a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: Someone swears at a person who is eating a cheese sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: The bleeped oath stands for a dismissive exclamation, and 'roll' is a bread roll, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A brioche is a soft, sweet, enriched French bread, often baked as a small individual bun.

clue.text: Wrinkled penis ... uses round end of iron ... waiting anxiously!

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept
something wrinkled is creased and crumpled, so its letters lose their shape
turning round suggests the letters are spun into a fresh order

blocks.note: five letters to be mixed
four letters to be mixed
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A smutty picture of someone using an iron to press out creases, nervously awaiting the result.
explanation.walkthrough: All ten letters, including the iron's final N, are rearranged together; the dots are only punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: Being kept in a state of nervous uncertainty about what will happen is the idiom's sense.

clue.text: (& 24ac.) New sort of discouragement, or else covering up sin ultimately: Weinstein's secret weapon?

indicators.note: to sort is to rearrange, so these letters are put into a fresh order
to cover something is to wrap around it, so one piece encloses another
ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
fourteen letters for the mix
six more letters for the mix
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A topical jibe: gagging contracts were a new kind of deterrent, covering up the sins of Harvey Weinstein.
explanation.walkthrough: The mixed letters wrap around the N from 'sin', placed after NO. Harvey Weinstein, the disgraced film producer, used gagging contracts to silence accusers.
explanation.definitionFit: Such contracts legally bound victims to silence, hiding the producer's abuse for years; a cynical description of a gagging clause.

clue.text: Cry "Piss off!" when bored by European head

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter alone
a thing bored by a drill has something passing into it, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: scram is a curt order to go away
opening letter of the word

explanation.definitionFit: A scream is a loud, piercing shout, so the noun or verb matches a loud outburst.

clue.text: The shot tale of a celeb?

blocks.clueFragment: The shot tale of a celeb?

setter's reading: a life story that has been filmed, shot by a camera

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' suggests gunfire and an assassinated star; in film-making a scene is shot, so it is a filmed life story.

clue.text: About time lefties outed, if going for a seat

about means around, so one piece is wrapped around another

the two letters that leave

explanation.walkthrough: 'A seat' looks like a place in Parliament, but a settle is a wooden bench. 'Outed' sounds like exposing someone; here it scrambles what is left.

clue.text: Mistakenly elected – dread being without leader

blocks.note: a candidate who is elected is in

explanation.walkthrough: 'Elected' sounds like part of the political story, but it just means 'in', as when a candidate gets in.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something by mistake is doing it wrongly, through an oversight or a wrong judgment.

clue.text: TV show presenter takes on mature detainee?

blocks.note: the person who fronts a television programme
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: A television presenter signs up an older contestant who may be a prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mature' looks like an adjective for the detainee, but it is a verb meaning grow older.
explanation.definitionFit: A person held captive against their will as security for demands is a kind of prisoner.

clue.text: Where to learn to move the earth?
